title: OPS-GATED: domain-check has never been deployed to apexalgo-iad -- ArgoCD sync blocked by stray kustomization.yaml
description:
docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20) explicitly flagged: "the service currently has no live deployment at all -- no ArgoCD Application is registered for domain-check in declarative-config and the ronaldraygun/domain-check Docker Hub repository has never had an image pushed to it." Confirmed still true today (2026-07-30), and no bead in this workspace (193 total, searched terms: deploy, ArgoCD Application, apexalgo, kustomization, namespace) tracks it -- this is a live, unfiled gap.

Root cause found: `kubectl --server=http://traefik-apexalgo-iad:8001 get namespace domain-check` returns NotFound. The ArgoCD Application named domain-check-ns-apexalgo-iad (namespace argocd on ardenone-manager) exists but has been stuck OutOfSync / health Missing since creation, condition SyncError: "one or more synchronization tasks are not valid (retried 2 times)." Its resource list shows a phantom resource -- "Kustomization None OutOfSync None" -- alongside the real 8 (Namespace, ConfigMap, Deployment, Service, ServiceMonitor, IngressRoute, 2 Middlewares), all stuck Missing.

Cause: in the declarative-config repo, the domain-check manifest directory (under the apexalgo-iad cluster folder) contains a kustomization.yaml file, but the apexalgo-iad ApplicationSet (manifest file named apexalgo-iad-applicationset.yml, same cluster folder) generates this Application with a plain-directory source (directory: recurse true, include "{*.yaml,*.yml}"), not a Kustomize source. ArgoCD's plain-manifest renderer therefore treats kustomization.yaml as a literal manifest and tries to apply kind: Kustomization directly, which is invalid -- and that single invalid task fails the ENTIRE sync, so even the Namespace itself never gets created. Corroborating evidence in the same repo: the mta-my-way app (also under apexalgo-iad) has its own kustomization.yaml and shows the identical symptom (mta-my-way-ns-apexalgo-iad: OutOfSync/Degraded), and the iad-ci argo-workflows manifests already contain a kustomization.yaml.disabled -- proof this exact failure mode was found and worked around once before by disabling the file.

Fix (in declarative-config, a DIFFERENT repo -- not this one):
1. Remove (or rename to .disabled) the kustomization.yaml in domain-check's manifest directory; fold its "namespace: domain-check" setting and commonLabels into the individual manifest files if still wanted (the rest of this repo's convention is flat plain manifests, no Kustomize -- see the k8s conventions doc in declarative-config).
2. Separately, domain-check's deployment.yaml pins image: ronaldraygun/domain-check:latest, which violates declarative-config's own explicit rule (never :latest for ronaldraygun images) -- must be pinned to a semver tag once a real image has been built and pushed (blocked on the CI quality-gate actually passing -- see the related bead about the unpushed fix).
3. Commit + push to declarative-config, let ArgoCD re-sync, confirm the domain-check Application reaches Synced/Healthy and the domain-check namespace/pods actually appear on apexalgo-iad.

OPS-GATED because: the fix lives in declarative-config (a different repo governing live cluster state) and will cause ArgoCD to create real resources on the apexalgo-iad production cluster -- must go through the mandated declarative-config commit, push, ArgoCD sync flow, and needs judgment about sequencing against the still-unresolved CI/image-availability issue.

comments.text:
## Quality-Gate Root Cause Analysis (from bf-68gr)

**Exit code:** 2 (non-zero exit from the shell step)

**Failing command:** `go test -race ./...`

**Root cause:** CGO is disabled on `golang:1.26-alpine`. The `-race` flag requires `CGO_ENABLED=1` because Go's race detector is implemented in C. The error message is:
`go: -race requires cgo; enable cgo by setting CGO_ENABLED=1`

**Classification:** NOT a go vet error, NOT a test failure, NOT a compilation error. This is a **build environment configuration error** — the CI image doesn't support the race detector.

**go vet ./...** passed successfully (all 19 dependencies downloaded, no issues found).

**No specific packages failed** — the failure occurs before any tests run, at the Go toolchain level.

**Fix options (in WorkflowTemplate `domain-check-build`):**
1. Add `CGO_ENABLED=1` env + `apk add build-base` (gcc/musl-dev) to quality-gate step
2. Switch image from `golang:1.26-alpine` to `golang:1.26` (Debian, CGO works OOTB)
3. Drop `-race` (not recommended — plan.md specifies race detector as CI guarantee)

Full logs saved in `docs/notes/quality-gate-logs-2026-07-04.md`.

comments.text:
## Root Cause Analysis — bf-68gr

### Exit Code
**2** — Go toolchain usage error (not a test failure which would be exit code 1).

### Failure Classification
**Configuration/Infrastructure issue** — the quality-gate step uses golang:1.26-alpine which disables CGO by default, but runs go test -race which requires CGO.

### Failing Command
go test -race ./...

### Error Message (verbatim)
go: -race requires cgo; enable cgo by setting CGO_ENABLED=1

### Passing Commands
- apk --no-cache add git ca-certificates — OK
- git clone --branch main — OK
- go vet ./... — OK (no vet errors)
- All dependencies downloaded successfully

### No Test Failures
No Go tests were executed. The failure occurs at the toolchain level before any test code is compiled. The -race flag is rejected by the go command itself because CGO_ENABLED=0 on Alpine (musl libc).

### Root Cause
On Alpine images, CGO_ENABLED defaults to 0. The race detector requires CGO because it instruments memory accesses using C-level atomics. go test -race exits immediately with exit code 2.

### Source
Logs captured from debug workflow domain-check-build-debug-podgc2-5dxln (podGC: OnWorkflowSuccess). Full logs saved to docs/quality-gate-logs.md and docs/quality-gate-root-cause.md. All 5+ consecutive failed runs show identical main: Error (exit code 2).

### Consistent Across Runs
domain-check-build-jxwhw, domain-check-build-hsrx2, domain-check-build-45dk7, domain-check-build-debug-qg-wl5sw, domain-check-build-debug-qg-h89zn — all fail with exit code 2 from the same root cause.

title: Fix regression: parse.go rejects private-suffix domains, contradicting plan.md edge case #45 (already re-verified by closed bf-2vg2)

Rationale given: PSL PRIVATE-section suffix; publicsuffix.PublicSuffix() returns icann=false but Parse() should still accept it, only rejected downstream as unsupported_tld if no RDAP/WHOIS server covers the TLD. This was independently re-verified and closed as correct by bead bf-2vg2 ("plan.md edge case #45 already accurately describes implementation... Parse() accepts private-suffix domains... No changes needed").

However, internal/domain/parse.go currently has a Step 6 block (~lines 97-108, comment "Reject PSL private-suffix domains") that does the OPPOSITE: `if !icann && strings.Contains(tld, ".") { return nil, &ParseError{... Phase: "private-suffix" ...} }`. title: go test ./... (no flags) times out after 10min -- gate long-running memory/benchmark tests behind explicit opt-in
description:
Running `go test ./...` exactly as documented in this repo's CLAUDE.md Development section (no flags) does not complete: the internal/server package fails after Go's default 600s per-package test timeout, dumping a goroutine trace rooted in `runMemoryGrowthTest` (internal/server/memory_test.go:275/290). Reproduced directly on the lab server: `cd ~/domain-check && go test ./...` ran internal/server for 600.015s then FAILed.

Root cause: TestMemoryGrowthUnderLoad (30s), TestMemoryGrowthUnderLoadExtended (2m), TestMemoryGrowthUnderLoadFull (10m) in internal/server/memory_test.go, plus TestBenchmark_SustainedLoadP99 (10s), TestBenchmark_SustainedLoadP99_Long (30s), TestBenchmark_ConcurrentBulkP99 (5s) in internal/server/benchmark_regression_test.go, are ONLY skipped when `testing.Short()` is true, i.e. only under `go test -short`. Run without `-short` -- the documented default -- these run sequentially and the memory tests alone total ~12.5 minutes, exceeding Go's 600s per-package timeout.

This plausibly explains repeated timeouts for autonomous workers/agents that run the documented default test command against this repo.

Note: this is a DIFFERENT issue from the already-tracked quality-gate CI failure (bf-25p4/bf-m84x chain, see docs/notes/quality-gate-failure-analysis.md) -- that one is a `go test -race` link-time failure caused by CGO being disabled on the Alpine CI image, and fails before any test executes. This bead is about plain `go test ./...` (no -race) hanging on long-running tests that only check `-short`. Do not conflate the two or fold this into that chain.

Fix approach: change the guard in all 6 long-running tests from `if testing.Short() { t.Skip(...) }` to an explicit opt-in env var, e.g. `if os.Getenv("DOMCHECK_RUN_LONG_TESTS") != "1" { t.Skip("set DOMCHECK_RUN_LONG_TESTS=1 to run") }`. Document the env var in CLAUDE.md and docs/benchmarks/README.md. Keep `-short` behavior (still skips) so existing short-mode CI/dev flows are unaffected.

Acceptance criteria:
- `go test ./...` (zero flags, zero env vars) completes in well under 5 minutes across all packages, exit code 0
- `DOMCHECK_RUN_LONG_TESTS=1 go test ./internal/server/... -run TestMemoryGrowthUnderLoadFull -timeout 15m` still runs the full test on demand
- `go test -short ./...` behavior unchanged

The actual CSP set in both web/templates/layout.html (meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy") and internal/server/middleware.go's SecurityHeaders (~line 129) is: default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; -- note style-src carries 'unsafe-inline', undermining the plan's stated "no inline anything" CSP posture.

Root cause: web/templates/result.html has two inline style="..." attributes -- around line 35: `<h2 style="margin-bottom: 1rem; font-size: 1.1rem; color: var(--color-text-secondary);">` and around line 50: `<div class="registration-details" style="margin-top: 1rem;">` -- that require 'unsafe-inline' to render without a CSP violation.

Fix: move both inline style rules into web/static/style.css as named classes (e.g. a heading modifier class and a spacing modifier class) and reference them via class= instead of style= in result.html. Once no inline style="..." attributes remain anywhere under web/templates/, remove 'unsafe-inline' from style-src in BOTH web/templates/layout.html's CSP meta tag and internal/server/middleware.go's SecurityHeaders CSP string (keep the two in sync -- they must match). Do not otherwise touch the plan's other CSP deltas (img-src data:, font-src 'self', connect-src 'self') -- those appear to be legitimate, necessary additions for the fetch-based JS and are out of scope here; only remove 'unsafe-inline'. Acceptance: `grep -n 'style="' web/templates/*.html` returns no matches; style-src in both layout.html and middleware.go no longer contains 'unsafe-inline'; `go test ./internal/server/...` passes; manually loading /check?d=example.com in a browser shows no CSP console errors.

Commit f6178ab ("chore: remove orphaned internal/bootstrap and internal/httpclient packages") tore out an earlier attempt at exactly the CLAUDE.md-described split after it left the build broken (independently confirmed: checking out the pre-revert tree, i.e. current origin/main, and running go vet ./... fails with 3 undefined-symbol errors across internal/bootstrap, internal/httpclient, and internal/checker's test files).

Its descendant chain (bf-10sy "Extract SSRF-safe HTTP client into internal/httpclient", bf-9j9u "Update all imports and slim internal/checker to orchestrator-only", bf-5hr0 "Extract WHOIS client into internal/whois package", all currently blocked) is chasing a goal a past agent already tried and explicitly abandoned. A second, independently mitosis-split ~17-bead chain (bf-2ru -> bf-5vp -> bf-2ob -> bf-5oq -> bf-3bd -> bf-259 -> bf-4wvi -> bf-4u8b -> bf-31nu -> bf-iotu -> bf-5ti6 -> bf-35v3 -> bf-1csr -> bf-4k8v -> bf-m84x -> bf-25p4) has also been chasing the same underlying broken-refactor symptom under the banner of "why does quality-gate fail," and is likewise stuck (bf-25p4 is deferred + verification-failed, failure-count:4). Fix: (1) update CLAUDE.md's Package Layout section to describe the actual, current, intentionally-consolidated internal/checker/ structure (or explicitly mark the split as a rejected/superseded direction with a one-line note, so future agents do not re-derive bf-1hs from it again); (2) once updated, bf-1hs and its entire blocked descendant chain can be closed as superseded -- the architecture they target is not the intended one.

title: Recent-checks history (localStorage) is write-only -- never rendered in the UI
description:
plan.md "Progressive Enhancement (with JS)" section (~lines 288-293) lists "History of recent checks (localStorage, never sent to server)" as a shipped feature. web/static/app.js implements ld() (load history from localStorage key 'domain-check-history') and sv() (save/dedupe an entry, cap at 20 via constant M=20) -- sv() is invoked after every rendered result via card()/rM(). However, ld() is called ONLY from inside sv()'s own body (for de-duplication before saving) -- grep 'ld()' in web/static/app.js shows exactly the definition plus that one internal call. Nothing ever reads the saved history back out to render it: grep -n 'history' across web/templates/*.html and web/static/style.css returns no matches at all. So domain-check silently accumulates a browser-local check history that the user can never see or click into -- the feature is write-only / half-built.

Fix: add a "Recent checks" UI section (e.g. rendered by app.js on page load into index.html, reading ld()) showing the last N saved entries (domain + available/taken status) as links to /check?d=<domain>, plus a simple way to clear the history. Keep it 100% client-side per the plan's privacy framing ("never sent to server") -- no new server-side code or endpoints needed, this is a JS + template + CSS change only. Ensure it degrades gracefully with JS disabled (matches the rest of app.js's progressive-enhancement pattern -- no history section should render without JS). Add or extend a Playwright test in tests/e2e/web-ui.spec.ts asserting that after checking a domain, reloading the home page shows it in a visible, clickable recent-checks list. Acceptance: Playwright test passes; manual verification that a checked domain appears in a visible history list after checking it and reloading the home page.
